Part A — Murrell-style Recap

Below are a few minimal base R snippets to revisit Murrell’s ideas.

Code 
# Simple base plot + text
plot(pressure, pch = 16)
text(150, 600, "Pressure (mm Hg)\nversus\nTemperature (Celsius)")
Code 
# Histogram example
set.seed(123)
Y <- rnorm(50)
Y[Y < -3.5 | Y > 3.5] <- NA
hist(Y, breaks = seq(-3.5,3.5,0.5), freq = FALSE, col = "gray80")
curve(dnorm(x), add = TRUE, lwd = 2)

Note : - pch sets point symbols (0–25; 21–25 respect bg), cex scales size, las controls axis label orientation.
- axis(side=...): 1 bottom, 2 left, 3 top, 4 right.
- par(mar=...): margins in lines as c(bottom,left,top,right).

Part B — With Happy Planet Dataset

We will create comparable visuals on your HPI data.

1) Scatter with smoother: GDP per capita vs Life Expectancy (latest year)

Code 
hp1 <- hp %>%
  mutate(
    LifeExp = as.numeric(LifeExp),
    `GDP per capita` = as.numeric(`GDP per capita`)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(LifeExp), !is.na(`GDP per capita`))

latest_year <- max(hp1$Year, na.rm = TRUE)
hp_latest <- hp1 %>% filter(Year == latest_year)

# Base R version (Murrell-style)
plot(hp_latest$`GDP per capita`, hp_latest$LifeExp,
     pch = 19, cex = 0.7,
     xlab = "GDP per Capita",
     ylab = "Life Expectancy",
     main = paste0("HPI ", latest_year, ": GDP per Capita vs Life Expectancy"))
lines(lowess(hp_latest$`GDP per capita`, hp_latest$LifeExp, f = 0.5), lwd = 2)
Code 
# ggplot2 version (polished)
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(hp_latest, aes(x = `GDP per capita`, y = LifeExp)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, span = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("HPI ", latest_year, ": GDP per Capita vs Life Expectancy"),
    x = "GDP per Capita", y = "Life Expectancy"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

2) Histogram: Life Expectancy (latest year)

Code 
# Base R
hist(hp_latest$LifeExp, col = "gray85", border = "white",
     main = paste0("Life Expectancy — ", latest_year),
     xlab = "Years")
Code 
# ggplot2
ggplot(hp_latest, aes(x = LifeExp)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2) +
  labs(title = paste0("Life Expectancy — ", latest_year),
       x = "Years", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

3) Boxplot: Life Expectancy by Continent (latest year)

Code 
# Base R
boxplot(LifeExp ~ Continent, data = hp_latest,
        col = "gray80",
        main = paste0("Life Expectancy by Continent — ", latest_year),
        xlab = "Continent", ylab = "Life Expectancy")
Code 
# ggplot2
ggplot(hp_latest, aes(x = Continent, y = LifeExp)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = paste0("Life Expectancy by Continent — ", latest_year),
       x = "Continent", y = "Life Expectancy") +
  theme_minimal()

4) Barplot: Average HPI by Continent (latest year)

Code 
# Some rows may have missing HPI, coerce if needed
hp_latest2 <- hp %>%
  mutate(HPI = as.numeric(HPI)) %>%
  filter(Year == latest_year, !is.na(HPI))

avg_hpi <- hp_latest2 %>%
  group_by(Continent) %>%
  summarize(avg_HPI = mean(HPI, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Base R
bp <- barplot(avg_hpi$avg_HPI, names.arg = avg_hpi$Continent,
              col = "gray70", las = 2,
              main = paste0("Average HPI by Continent — ", latest_year),
              ylab = "Average HPI")
box()
Code 
# ggplot2
ggplot(avg_hpi, aes(x = Continent, y = avg_HPI)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = paste0("Average HPI by Continent — ", latest_year),
       x = "Continent", y = "Average HPI") +
  theme_minimal()

5) Pie chart: Population share by Continent (latest year)

Code 
hp_pop <- hp %>%
  filter(Year == latest_year) %>%
  group_by(Continent) %>%
  summarize(pop = sum(as.numeric(Population), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Base R pie (for assignment parity)
pct <- hp_pop$pop / sum(hp_pop$pop)
lbl <- paste0(hp_pop$Continent, " (", scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 0.1), ")")
pie(pct, labels = lbl, col = gray(seq(0.3, 1, length.out = length(pct))),
    main = paste0("Population Share by Continent — ", latest_year))

Note

  • Axis sides: 1=bottom, 2=left, 3=top, 4=right.
  • pch/cex/bg: symbol/size/fill (bg applies to pch 21–25).
  • par(mar=…): margins in lines (bottom, left, top, right).
  • Hist vs density: set freq=FALSE to overlay density curves on histograms.
  • Boxplots: boxwex controls width; at controls positions (for side-by-side).
  • Smoothers: base R lowess(); ggplot geom_smooth(method='loess').
